items.title: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks
items.summary: Recent advances in video generation have increased the demand for reliable watermarking for copyright protection, yet the robustness of video watermarks against removal attacks remains underexplored. Most watermark-removal methods originate from the image domain: signal optimization injects imperceptible pixel-domain perturbations, whereas generative resynthesis produces a visually similar instance through diffusion synthesis. When extended to videos, the former introduces temporally varying noise that causes visible flickering, while the latter regenerates fine-grained structures inconsistently across frames, leading to structural motion inconsistency. To evaluate video watermark robustness, we propose PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction framework that removes watermarks while preserving the original content and motion. PoseRegen first applies a temporally shared viewpoint transformation to disrupt watermark-bearing spatial patterns and then jointly reconstructs the transformed sequence with a pose-conditioned video model. A frozen video DiT processes the complete sequence with its reference-video latent, and full-sequence Flow Matching supervision keeps identity and background consistent across frames. To further preserve motion structure, we introduce a lightweight Pose-Conditioned Motion Consistency Adapter that adapts the frozen backbone to temporally ordered pose...

items.title: Mitigating Task Objective Conflicts for Continual Learning in Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: Recent advances in unified autoregressive (AR) models have enabled multimodal understanding (MMU) and text-to-image generation (T2I) within a single architecture. However, in continual learning settings, their divergent objectives can induce task interference, hindering knowledge preservation and adaptation to new tasks. In this work, we investigate \textbf{T}ask \textbf{O}bjective \textbf{C}onflict (TOC) through theoretical and empirical analyses, revealing conflicting optimization directions at the task level but complementary interactions at the token level. These findings suggest that continual adaptation requires mitigating task interference while preserving beneficial cross-task knowledge sharing. To this end, we propose \textbf{UniDecouple}, a selective decoupling framework based on a \textbf{T}ask-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{M}ixture-\textbf{o}f-\textbf{E}xperts (TA-MoE) architecture. Specifically, UniDecouple retains shared attention layers to preserve common contextual dependencies while introducing task-specific feed-forward network (FFN) experts to mitigate optimization conflicts. Furthermore, hierarchical expert routing enables adaptive expert selection, while hybrid expert collaboration leverages shared experts to facilitate cross-task knowledge transfer. A two-stage training strategy further balances task specialization and coordinated adaptation. Extensive...

items.title: FaithfulFaces: Pose-Faithful Facial Identity Preservation for Text-to-Video Generation
items.summary: Identity-preserving text-to-video generation (IPT2V) empowers users to produce diverse and imaginative videos with consistent human facial identity. Despite recent progress, existing methods often suffer from significant identity distortion under large facial pose variations or facial occlusions. In this paper, we propose FaithfulFaces, a pose-faithful facial identity preservation learning framework to improve IPT2V in complex dynamic scenes. The key of FaithfulFaces is a pose-shared identity aligner that refines and aligns facial poses across distinct views via a pose-shared dictionary and a pose variation-identity invariance constraint. By mapping single-view inputs into a global facial pose representation with explicit Euler angle embeddings, FaithfulFaces provides a pose-faithful facial prior that guides generative foundations toward robust identity-preserving generation. In particular, we develop a specialized pipeline to curate a high-quality video dataset featuring substantial facial pose diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FaithfulFaces achieves state-of-the-art performance, maintaining superior identity consistency and structural clarity even as pose changes and occlusions occur. items.title: BG-REAL: A Public Real-Data Anchored Benchmark for Background Manipulation Detection and Localization
items.summary: Background manipulation is a practical but under-specified image-forensics setting: the manipulated evidence can sit outside the salient foreground object, while many evaluations emphasize object-centric copy-move, splicing, or generic synthetic edits. We introduce BG-REAL, a public real-data anchored benchmark package for background manipulation detection and localization. The current release is built from Open Images V7 instance-segmentation sources and contains 7,000 processed samples over 1,200 source groups, including 6,000 public-data anchored samples and 1,000 synthetic control samples. BG-REAL covers six edit families, matched authentic controls, source-group splits, mask and leakage QA, 599 human-assisted quality-control rows, three completed external baselines (TruFor, MVSS-Net, and HiFi-Net), and five-seed model evaluation. Beyond aggregate accuracy, we use matched-authentic-control diagnostics to measure how often baselines misclassify re-encoded authentic images as manipulated at a threshold fixed on held-out validation data; false-positive rates range from 0.57 (TruFor, the lowest) to 1.00 (several weak or mask-informed baselines), indicating that re-encoding artifacts are a shared shortcut risk across baselines rather than a problem specific to any one model. The release provides the construction pipeline, evaluation protocol, paper-ready figures, and...

items.title: Harmful YouTube Video Detection: A Taxonomy of Online Harm and MLLMs as Alternative Annotators
items.summary: Video platforms, used by billions globally, are criticized for exposing users to harmful content. Yet, detecting online harm remains challenging due to inconsistent approaches to what constitutes harm and limitations of human annotation. We address both challenges. Theoretically, we integrate and expand existing taxonomies and platform guidelines to multimodal contexts and develop a comprehensive taxonomy for online harm. We categorize online harm on video platforms into six content-based categories: Information, Hate and harassment, Addictive, Clickbait, Sexual, and Physical harms. Methodologically, we propose and systematically test multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as alternative annotators of harmful videos. We curate a dataset of 19,422 potentially harmful YouTube videos and annotate them using GPT-4-Turbo, non-trained crowdworkers, and trained annotators. We discuss the potential applications of MLLMs in platform content moderation and social science research, particularly in contexts where they perform comparably to human annotators in binary and multi-label classification tasks.

items.title: CoatFusion: Controllable Material Coating in Images
items.summary: We introduce Material Coating, a novel image editing task that simulates applying a thin material layer onto an object while preserving its underlying coarse and fine geometry. Material coating is fundamentally different from existing "material transfer" methods, which are designed to replace an object's intrinsic material, often overwriting fine details. To address this new task, we construct a large-scale synthetic dataset (110K images) of 3D objects with varied, physically-based coatings, named DataCoat110K. We then propose CoatFusion, a novel architecture that enables this task by conditioning a diffusion model on both a 2D albedo texture and granular, PBR-style parametric controls, including roughness, metalness, transmission, and a key thickness parameter. Experiments and user studies show CoatFusion produces realistic, controllable coatings and significantly outperforms existing material editing and transfer methods on this new task.

items.title: Learning to Reason About Implicit Multimodal Harm: From Diagnosis to Generalization
items.summary: A benign image paired with a benign caption can become harmful only in combination, making detection fundamentally a cross-modal reasoning problem. Existing multimodal harm benchmarks evaluate only classification accuracy, leaving unclear whether models identify the cross-modal mechanism that produces harm. We introduce MuPHI (Multimodal Pragmatic Harm Interpretation), a controlled diagnostic benchmark in which harm arises purely from image-text composition, with benign counterfactuals and annotated harm rationales. Using MuPHI, we systematically evaluate where compositional harm reasoning breaks in vision-language models (VLMs). MuPHI reveals that VLMs reliably ground each modality yet fail to bind the evidence into the harm mechanism and their predictions respond weakly to label-determining counterfactual interventions. Moreover, existing harm detection approaches trained on labels substantially improves in-domain (ID) detection but transfers poorly across harm distributions. We therefore propose Compositional Harm Interpretation Learning (CHIL), which rewards evidence identification in each modality, cross-modal binding and verdict consistency in the reasoning chain rather than just predicted label. CHIL improves 81% OOD transfer evaluations by an average of +2.5 macro-F1 and correct counterfactual flip rate by up to +3.8 and +5.4 % points, while also improving overall...

items.title: When Plans Change, Remember: Replanning-Guided Visual Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Long-horizon, multi-stage Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory. We introduce RePlanMem-VLA (Replanning-Guided Keyframe Memory for VLA), which turns a policy's own plan revisions into an online memory-write signal. Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. RePlanMem-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task-relevant event. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. The resulting detectors achieve ROC-AUC of 0.981-0.997. We then use the selected signals in RePlanMem-VLA to trigger updates to a bounded visual memory, with a robot-masked write filter suppressing redundant frames. In the evaluated memory-retention experiments, RePlanMem-VLA preserves task-relevant observations until the later decision point in 100% of episodes. Real-robot replay data further show that event selection and redundancy suppression extend beyond simulation...

items.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly...

items.title: Frechet Forcing: Training Long-Horizon Streaming World Models from Short Clips
items.summary: Streaming video world models generate the future chunk by chunk, conditioned on their own past and a stream of actions. Trained on short clips, they drift once a rollout exceeds the training horizon, as prediction errors re-enter the context and compound. A common remedy is to train the model on its own rollouts via distribution matching distillation (DMD). For action-conditioned world models, the teacher becomes a bottleneck: an external video model is agnostic to the actions, whereas the model's own pretrained network drifts in the same manner as the student. We observe that a long rollout need not match a teacher, provided it remains a realistic continuation of its own scene that follows the commanded actions. Realism and scene fidelity can be measured against real-data statistics, which remain valid at any horizon, while action following is preserved by the model's conditional generation loss. We propose Fr\'echet Forcing, which fine-tunes a world model together with its deployed multi-step sampler under three constraints. Generative anchoring applies the flow-matching loss after a self-generated history ending on real data. Context fidelity, a Fr\'echet distance (FD) on latent statistics of the free rollout centred on each clip's own ground truth, keeps every rollout faithful to its scene. Reality matching, an FD to real frames in a frozen perceptual space, keeps the...

items.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
items.summary: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene. However, navigation alone does not ensure that an action follows persistent rules when its outcome depends on state that is invisible in the current frame. We present Stateful Harness, a framework that separates world evolution from video rendering to support stateful and rule-governed interaction. It maintains an evolving world state under specified rules, renders each resulting event with a frozen video model, and uses the generated clip to update the world state for the next turn. At each turn, the harness resolves the action selected by the user and compiles the resulting event into an instruction, while a preview clip from an editable 3D scene provides spatial and camera guidance. To evaluate rule compliance, we build WorldState-Bench, a benchmark of 50 counterfactual twin pairs that share an initial frame and action but differ in hidden state and required outcome. Under rule-only prompting, the best of the 11 evaluated video backends produces the required endings for both cases in 32% of pairs. For MiniMax-H3, specifying the required endings raises this rate from 32% to 64%, while the full harness reaches 92% with the same frozen model. items.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
items.summary: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only as an environment with which the model can interact through actions (e.g., move left) and observations (rendered images). Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question. The model can then iteratively reason, navigate, and reorient its viewpoint before committing to a final answer. Following an initial trajectory-supervised finetuning, we apply reinforcement learning (RL) with rewards driven primarily by final-answer correctness. Crucially, RL provides no direct supervision over which viewpoints the model should visit or which exploration actions it should take. Instead, the model must learn an effective exploration policy solely from the extent to which its interactions improve performance. Across six 3D benchmarks, our model ACT3D achieves an average accuracy of 53.2% that improves its base Qwen model by 22.0% and surpasses proprietary Gemini 3.6 Flash. items.title: Improving Policy Learning via Language-Guided State Representation in World Models
items.summary: World models have emerged as powerful technology for facilitating policy learning in robotics by providing predictive representations of environmental dynamics. A crucial component of such models is the internal state representation, which serves as a bridge between observation, decision-making, and future state prediction. However, in multi-task settings, the presence of task-irrelevant information within the representation, especially under limited information capacity, can significantly impair the effectiveness of policy learning. To address this challenge, we propose Language-Guided State Representation (LGSR), a novel method that leverages language-based task descriptions as priors to guide the encoding of state representations within the world model. By incorporating language instructions, LGSR promotes the extraction of task-relevant features while suppressing irrelevant information, thereby enhancing the alignment between representation learning and task objectives. We evaluate LGSR on the CALVIN benchmark, a suite of language-conditioned robotic manipulation tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating language priors into the state representation enhances the extraction of task-relevant information, thereby significantly improving the efficiency and success rate of downstream policy learning.

items.title: EMMA: Event-Driven Multimodal Memory System with Multi-Agent Retrieval
items.summary: Long video understanding requires reasoning over hours of content that far exceed the context window of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Existing approaches compress video into fixed-length clips, yet events are fragmented and unrelated content is merged, yielding noisy retrieval. To overcome this challenge, we propose EMMA, an Event-driven Multimodal Memory system with Multi-Agent retrieval, which organizes memory around semantic events in three stages: (1) Event segmentation: a dual-stream detector adaptively locates event boundaries by fusing visual semantic drift with spoken transitions, rather than fixed windows. (2) Memory construction: built on the detected events, a three-level hierarchy of raw video, clip-level memory, and event-level memory stores content at progressively higher semantic abstraction. (3) Memory retrieval: a multi-agent framework collaboratively queries this hierarchy through query decomposition, tiered search, evidence validation, and answer generation, narrowing evidence from coarse events to precise clips. Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements, showing the effectiveness of our event-aligned memory system. Code, prompt templates, and reproduction scripts are available at https://github.com/BAI-LAB/EMMA.

items.title: Instance-Specific Classifier-Free Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion/Flow-Based Editing
items.summary: In recent years, a variety of prompt-based image editing methods have been developed based on text-to-image (T2I) diffusion/flow models. Image editing introduces an inherent trade-off between adhering to the original source image and realizing the change specified by the target prompt, which are typically measured by the LPIPS and CLIP-T metrics, respectively. Intuitively, this trade-off can be controlled by the classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale. Most existing editing methods, though, use a fixed CFG scale, ignoring that different edits require varying levels of modification. In this paper, we first explore the potential benefits of using an instance-specific CFG by exhaustively re-running prominent editing methods with a wide range of CFG scale values on benchmark datasets. We show that instance-specific setting can significantly improve LPIPS without compromising CLIP-T. Yet, tuning based on repeatedly executing an editing pipeline is inefficient. To prevent slow inference, we train a light-weight neural network that predicts the metrics of the underlying editing method for a given edit instance and CFG scale. At inference time, these predictions enable fast selection of an instance-specific CFG scale. Experiments across multiple editing methods and benchmark settings show the performance advantage of our approach over the baseline methods.

items.title: Cross-Modal Forgetting and Transfer in Unified Multimodal Post-Training
items.summary: Unified multimodal models answer questions about images and also generate images with one shared set of weights. This creates a post-training risk that single-purpose models do not have: fine-tuning one capability can damage another that works in a different modality. We measure this cross-modal forgetting for LoRA post-training of Janus-Pro-7B. Every target is chosen by how poorly the base model already handles it, from a poetic register to a language it barely speaks, so that retention is tested against a real intervention; we then evaluate the capabilities we never trained, first after a single run and then after chaining three. A single run looks entirely safe: nothing we did not train degrades on four public benchmarks or in free-form English, even when the adapter cuts held-out Welsh perplexity by 76% with a relative weight change under 2%. That safety belongs to the run, not to the recipe. Chaining three runs destroys the capability learned one run earlier and raises general-text perplexity by one to two orders of magnitude above the never-adapted model, on the very measures that stayed flat before. The cause is in the objective, which constrains only the modality being trained and leaves the other head unconstrained: cutting the learning rate to one fifth does not prevent the collapse, while anchoring the other head removes the damage to the capabilities we never...

items.title: Single-Pass Decision Scores Enable Rapid Classification with Adjustable Thresholds in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer binary clinical questions with a yes or no token, leaving the decision threshold implicit and fixed. We derive a continuous score from a single forward pass by renormalizing the probabilities of the yes and no tokens, allowing the threshold to be adapted to clinical needs without retraining. We evaluated this approach with MedGemma and Gemma-3 (4B and 27B) on six medical imaging datasets. The default threshold was frequently misaligned with the task: for identifying normal chest radiographs, MedGemma-27B labeled every image as abnormal, whereas a validation-selected threshold yielded a sensitivity of 0.945 and a specificity of 0.696. Normalization achieved the highest AUROC on four of six datasets (CheXpert: 0.819 vs. 0.777 for raw and 0.743 for text-elicited probabilities), and a single decision required 53-79 ms on one GPU. This simple post-hoc method turns medical MLLMs into fast classifiers with adjustable operating points. Code: https://github.com/TruhnLab/llm-threshold-calibration

items.title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
items.summary: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

items.title: Goal Images Are Control Targets: Spatially-Grounded Goal-Image Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Goal-conditioned manipulation policies are steered by a goal image, a picture of the desired post-manipulation scene synthesized from the current observation and a language instruction. The prevailing assumption is that better image-editing quality yields better goals, so goal generators are built and compared using general image-editing metrics. We show this assumption is false. Across two independent goal-conditioned policies on CALVIN, the image editors that top aggregate editing-quality leaderboards (Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5) produce worse control targets than our proposed far smaller finetuned open models, and the gap widens sharply for the multi-step (long-horizon) tasks robots actually face. A per-dimension analysis explains why. Downstream policy success is governed almost entirely by manipulation adherence (selecting the right object and the right final state; Spearman $\rho \approx 0.9$ with success), while photorealism and aesthetic fidelity, precisely where large proprietary editors excel, are uncorrelated with success ($\rho \approx 0$). This dissociation holds on both CALVIN and the real-world-aligned SIMPLER-Bridge benchmark. We then present SGE-Goal, a spatially-grounded decomposed editing framework that predicts initial and final 2D edit-region masks before goal-image synthesis. items.title: ReTrace: Visual Backtracking for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) encode images into dense visual token sequences, creating substantial attention and KV-cache overhead. Existing visual token compression methods reduce this cost by pruning low-saliency tokens in shallow layers, but this practice couples temporary computational deactivation with irreversible information deletion. We show that this coupling breaks an intrinsic inference pattern in MLLMs. Through layer-wise attention analysis, we identify \textbf{Visual Backtracking}: visual pivots remain spatially stable, yet in middle layers they actively retrieve context from tokens that appeared unimportant earlier. Thus, early low-saliency tokens can be inactive for computation while still being useful for later reasoning. Motivated by this finding, we propose \textbf{ReTrace}, a backtracking-aware compression framework that introduces a dormant token state. ReTrace caches non-pivot tokens outside expensive layer-wise computation, restores them during the backtracking window, and prunes only after their information has been absorbed. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 demonstrate nearly 90\% reductions in FLOPs and KV cache, a 2.83$\times$ prefilling speedup, and strong performance retention across complex vision-language benchmarks.

items.title: PLANE: Plug-and-Play Fine-Grained Visual Experts for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) commonly suffer from hallucinations, which appear as fabricating non-existent objects or outputting incorrect attributes and spatial relationships in images. Previous works empirically indicate that CLIP-style vision encoders tend to focus on primary objects while ignoring image details, which is one of the causes of hallucinations. To address this issue, we propose plug-and-play fine-grained visual experts (PLANE) comprising two components: LoRA visual experts operating on CLIP for multi-aspect image encoding, and an instruction-aware gate network for adaptive image feature fusion. During training, we construct a fine-grained image-caption pairs dataset, where images are described from three aspects: objects, attributes, and relations between objects. Image-caption pairs from different aspects are used to train the three fine-grained LoRA experts respectively. Aiming at comprehensively evaluate our method's capabilities, we manually annotate a fine-grained hallucination evaluation benchmark for LVLMs which is GPT4-independent during evaluation phase (GIFT). We conduct experiments both on popular hallucination evaluation benchmarks and GIFT. The results show that our method effectively reduces hallucinations across models of different types and sizes while introducing minimal inference latency. items.title: From Label Priors to Task Evidence: Efficient Long-Video Frame Selection via Bayesian GRPO
items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Existing retrieval-based approaches typically rely on supervised learning from static keyframe annotations. However, these label priors often fail to align with the actual information required by downstream MLLMs for complex reasoning, creating a misalignment between the training target and inference needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a probabilistic framework that reformulates frame selection as latent-variable inference. We first initialize a lightweight policy using supervised learning to capture general visual saliency. Then, we treat a frozen MLLM as a task environment and use its answer likelihood as dense task evidence to refine the policy via Bayesian Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Within this formulation, the negative log-likelihood (NLL) over ground-truth answer tokens provides a principled dense reward, while a prior-matching KL term preserves semantic consistency with the elicited label prior. This process transitions the selection principle from static label priors to task evidence. items.title: Clean Forcing: Drift-Resistant Autoregressive Video Diffusion with a Frozen Base
items.summary: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate streaming video of arbitrary length by conditioning each new chunk of frames on those already generated. However, they suffer from exposure bias, where a model trained on clean context must continue from its own imperfect outputs, and errors compound until quality collapses within seconds (drift). Existing methods either require cluster-scale base retraining, apply training-free inference corrections with inconsistent results, or train frozen-base correctors for sampling and cache errors. We instead find that drift is largely deterministic and therefore learnable, as holding the noisy state fixed while varying only the history reveals a counterfactual velocity gap that is ~95% systematic across noise seeds. Based on this observation, we introduce Clean Forcing, which trains a 5.9M-parameter LoRA corrector on the frozen base model to regress this gap, with a closed-loop stage that adds DAgger-style aggregation and a drift-contraction objective to expose the corrector to its own rollouts. Because the clean histories can be the base model's own single-shot generations, training needs no real videos, and the merged corrector adds no inference cost. items.title: SAPO: Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization for Improving Temporal Video Grounding in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Video vision-language models (VLMs) have strong semantic understanding, yet remain unreliable at precise temporal grounding. Existing gains from explicitly aligning video frames with absolute time suggest that VLMs may already encode accurate temporal locations internally but lose precision when expressing them as timestamps. Our analysis across four VLMs and two grounding datasets confirms this hypothesis: attention intervals outperform predicted intervals on approximately 66% of valid examples. We term this discrepancy the temporal generation gap. Because precise temporal annotations are expensive, this finding motivates closing the gap to improve temporal grounding using only unlabeled video-query pairs. We propose Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses internal temporal attention as self-supervision for Group Relative Policy Optimization and applies a ground-truth-free criterion to select high-value samples. SAPO consistently improves temporal grounding across multiple datasets and models spanning weak to strong initial grounding ability. Relative mIoU gains reach 33.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 5.4% on the strong Time-R1-7B. The improvements transfer across datasets while preserving general video understanding.

items.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
items.summary: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark. The LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline we measured, 82.21 F1 on the adversarial split, sat 1.21 to 8.67 points above the adversarial baselines we planned to compare against (81.00, 79.30, and 73.54). We looked at the evaluation code and found a readout choice that moves F1 on its own. A two-token logit readout decides yes versus no by comparing two vocabulary IDs, 3582 ("yes") and 1217 ("no"). Across 9,000 greedy-decode questions spanning all three splits, neither ID is generated even once. The model emits " Yes" (token 3869) and " No" (token 1939), because SentencePiece prepends a space byte after the prompt suffix "ASSISTANT:". Read with an eight-token lookup that covers the space-prefixed surface forms, LLaVA-1.5-7B scores F1 0.8221, 0.8498, and 0.8713 on the adversarial, popular, and random splits. That 6.13-point adversarial shift exceeds the adversarial gain reported by five of the six papers we surveyed. None of them states its readout, and our reference ran under 4-bit NF4 quantization, so we cannot say how much of any reported gain a matched evaluation would keep. That comparison stays unresolved until readout and precision are matched. items.title: Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion
items.summary: Autoregressive Diffusion Transformers have emerged as a powerful paradigm for long video generation. However, they are often constrained by prohibitive computational overhead and substantial memory footprints. This inefficiency arises from dense computation mechanisms that allocate uniform processing resources across all spatiotemporal regions, failing to leverage the inherent temporal redundancy of video where motion is typically confined to sparse areas. In this paper, we propose Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention (DASA), a unified framework that shifts from dense computation to sparse, motion-driven generation to eliminate both storage and computational redundancies. Inspired by video codec principles, our approach explicitly decouples video content into dynamic and static regions. To mitigate memory bottlenecks, we selectively compress the historical KV cache by retaining only dynamic features within the generated chunk. Furthermore, to reduce computational overhead, we employ a region-level computation allocation strategy based on localized dynamics. Additionally, a dynamics-guided distillation method is introduced to enhance performance via a lightweight distillation training process. Experiments on VBench demonstrate that our approach accelerates autoregressive video generation by 2.16x, while preserving high visual fidelity.

items.title: From Cause to Effect: Generating Intermediate Event Chains in Videos
items.summary: Video-Language Models (VLMs) excel at visual recognition but struggle with causal reasoning. Current evaluations are flawed: multiple-choice QA allows shortcuts, and open-ended QA lacks robust automatic evaluation. We introduce Causal Chain Generation (CCG), a novel task where models have to generate the sequence of intermediate events connecting a cause and an effect. This structured setup demands genuine reasoning and enables reliable automatic scoring. We accompany this task with two complementary metrics: SODA-Embedding, which measures the semantic matching of a generated chain against a reference, and Causal-QA, which probes the chain's causal coherence by asking whether it contains the specific causal facts needed to reconstruct the narrative. We provide two test sets: SF20K-CC, a manually annotated diagnostic on 20 short films, and CMD-CC, a movie clip benchmark derived from audio descriptions. Our analysis reveals that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with narrative causality understanding, frequently hallucinating or omitting key events. To address this, we fine-tune VLMs with GRPO using a composite reward that combines a format reward, SODA-Embedding, and Causal-QA accuracy, demonstrating substantial improvements over strong baselines.

items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.summary: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. items.title: Cattle-CLIP: A Multimodal Framework for Dairy Cattle Behaviour Recognition from Video
items.summary: Monitoring cattle behaviour provides valuable insights into animal health, productivity and welfare. However, robust behaviour recognition in real-world farm environments remains challenging because well-annotated livestock video datasets are scarce and agricultural surveillance footage differs substantially from large-scale pretraining data. To address these challenges, we propose Cattle-CLIP, a domain-adaptive vision-language framework based on Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP), which reformulates cattle behaviour recognition as a cross-modal semantic alignment task. Cattle-CLIP incorporates a temporal integration module that extends image-level contrastive pretraining to video-based behaviour understanding and promotes consistent semantic alignment across time. To reduce domain discrepancy, customised data augmentation and behaviour-oriented prompts are employed. We also construct CattleBehaviours6, a curated dataset containing 1,905 annotated clips from six indoor behaviours: feeding, drinking, standing-self-grooming, standing-ruminating, lying-self-grooming and lying-ruminating. The dataset provides standardised ethogram definitions for model training, evaluation and future livestock behaviour research. items.title: Training Long-Context Vision-Language Models Effectively with Generalization Beyond 128K Context
items.summary: Long-context modeling is becoming a core capability of modern large vision-language models (LVLMs), enabling sustained context management across long-document understanding, video analysis, and multi-turn tool use in long-horizon agents. Yet practical training recipes remain insufficiently explored, particularly for designing and balancing long-context data mixtures. In this work, we present a systematic study of long-context continued pre-training (LongPT) for LVLMs, extending a 7B model from 32K to 128K context with extensive ablations on long-document data. We first show that long-document VQA is substantially more effective than OCR transcription. Building on this observation, our ablations further yield three key findings: i) for sequence-length distribution, balanced data outperforms target-length-focused data (e.g., 128K), suggesting that long-context ability requires generalizable key-information retrieval across various lengths and positions; ii) retrieval remains the primary bottleneck, favoring retrieval-heavy mixtures with modest reasoning data for task diversity; iii) pure long-document VQA largely preserves short-context capabilities, suggesting that instruction-formatted long data reduces the need for short-data mixing. items.title: Token-Budget Distillation: Transferring Full-Token Semantics to Compressed Video Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Adapting video vision-language models (VLMs) is computationally expensive because video inputs produce a large number of visual tokens, making both fine-tuning and inference costly. Although visual token compression can reduce this overhead, direct adaptation on compressed inputs often causes semantic drift and noticeable performance degradation. We present Token-Budget Distillation (TBD), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework for adapting video VLMs under a fixed token budget. TBD freezes the pretrained backbone, updates only LoRA adapters, and integrates FlashVID-based visual token compression into the video pathway. To preserve full-token semantics under compression, TBD employs a dual-path teacher-student design, where a full-token teacher provides stable supervision and a compressed student is optimized with task loss, answer-region KL distillation, GT-anchored margin distillation, and reliability-aware KD control. This design enables the student to recover the semantic behavior of the full-token model while remaining efficient under aggressive token reduction. We evaluate TBD on three video VLM backbones, including LLaVA-Video, LLaVA-OneVision, and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, across four video understanding benchmarks. TBD consistently outperforms compression-only baselines under both moderate and aggressive compression. On LLaVA-Video at retention ratio R = 10 percent...

items.title: Vision-language models see more about agriculture than they report, and test-time scaling remains bounded by parametric knowledge
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for agricultural diagnosis but fail unpredictably in zero-shot settings. We test whether this stems from poor visual features or an inability to verbalize what the model already perceives, using a benchmark spanning classification and detection drawn from 118 AgML classification and 54 detection datasets. Linear probing shows agricultural features are linearly separable in frozen VLM vision towers, with Gemma-4-31B's encoder reaching F1-macro of 0.60--0.78 across tasks and approaching the vision-only DINOv3 backbone, indicating the bottleneck lies downstream of perception. We then test whether test-time scaling, an iterative in-context skill-memory loop, can close this gap without updating weights. Gains are modest and inconsistent. Skill-memory improves classification accuracy by up to 3.1 points on three of four tasks while regressing on species, with gains concentrated on classes seen during optimization and unseen classes regressing. Detection F1 is effectively unchanged (0.412 to 0.421), though an oracle filtering condition reaches 0.432 F1, revealing real headroom unconstrained prompting fails to surface. items.title: MINER: Multi-crop INference-time Enhancement for Rare-Object Retrieval with Frozen Dual Encoders
items.summary: Text-to-image retrieval with frozen dual encoders degrades when the query names a small, visually subordinate object in a cluttered scene: a single global image embedding underrepresents the localized visual evidence. We present MINER, a training-free inference framework that augments a frozen dual encoder's global image embedding with a small bank of region-level embeddings and a hubness-correcting similarity rescoring, recovering visual evidence that global pooling underweights. To evaluate this setting, we introduce ROCS, a benchmark built from high-clutter subsets of Flickr30K and MS COCO whose images are re-captioned to name a single low-salience object. Experiments on CLIP, SigLIP, and SigLIP 2 show that MINER improves retrieval on every backbone, on ROCS and on the standard splits. Analyses show that these gains come primarily from broader spatial coverage rather than precise crop placement, revealing a simple and general way to recover localized evidence from frozen representations. items.title: Pushing the Frontier of Black-Box LVLM Attacks via Fine-Grained Detail Targeting
items.summary: Black-box adversarial attacks on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) are challenging due to missing gradients and complex multimodal boundaries. Prior state-of-the-art transfer-based approaches such as M-Attack match local crops between source and target images, but this induces high-variance, nearly orthogonal gradients across iterations. We attribute this instability to (i) ViT translation sensitivity, which yields spike-like gradients, and (ii) a structural asymmetry between source and target crops. We reformulate local matching as an asymmetric expectation over source transformations and target semantics, and introduce M-Attack-V2 based on this formulation. Multi-Crop Alignment (MCA) averages gradients from multiple local views per iteration, while Auxiliary Target Alignment (ATA) replaces aggressive target augmentation with a small set of semantically correlated auxiliary images. Patch Momentum replays historical crop gradients, and a patch-diverse surrogate ensemble (PE+) strengthens transferable directions. M-Attack-V2 raises attack success rates over M-Attack from 40% to 61% on GPT-6.1 Sol, from 40% to 60% on GPT-6 Astra, and from 85% to 97% on Claude Sonnet 5.5. Code and data are publicly available at: https://github.com/VILA-Lab/M-Attack-V2.

items.title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models
items.summary: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. items.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement
items.summary: We introduce Long Listening Thoughts (LLT), a framework for constructing post-training datasets that improves audio reasoning by pairing deliberate perceptual grounding with explicit cognitive behaviors. On audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks, large audio-language models (LALMs) are limited primarily by perceptual errors, yet existing post-training datasets rely on audio descriptions of limited diversity. Through a four-stage pipeline, LLT (1) builds multi-aspect dense audio descriptions spanning semantic, acoustic, and temporal information, (2) generates more challenging questions, (3) synthesizes incorrect reasoning traces, and (4) extends short reasoning traces into long ones via a thought-continuation strategy that elicits cognitive behaviors such as verification and backtracking. Using LLT, we synthesize 1.6M reasoning traces and train Qwen2.5-Omni-7B with a two-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). This improves accuracy on MMAU Test-mini (71.5 to 78.2), MMAR (56.7 to 63.7), and MMSU (60.6 to 66.0).

items.title: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Open resources for computer use agents (CUAs) -- environments, datasets, and models -- remain scattered: without a standard, these resources cannot be integrated and scaled; additionally, evaluation, RL, and SFT cannot share one infrastructure. We present CUA-Lite, an open platform for developing CUAs, built around three standardized abstractions: (1) Unified environment interface, under which we integrate 12 benchmarks across desktop, browser, and mobile, plus lightweight VM-free sandboxes that replicate OSWorld's desktop at much lower cost, providing over 30,000 verifiable tasks. (2) Unified supervised data format, into which we convert the major public CUA datasets, from GUI grounding and understanding to full rollouts, and record our fresh rollouts from frontier CUAs on these verifiable environments. (3) Model harnesses shared across evaluation, RL, and SFT, one per model and implemented for 14 model families. Each harness runs its model in these computer environments, producing the rollouts that evaluation and RL consume, or renders stored supervised data into the model's own training format for SFT. We release reference scores across the integrated benchmarks, and show that RL and SFT through the same harness improve open-weight models. We release our dataset, code, and models, and the platform is open to contributions.

items.title: Planning Takes More Than Token Prediction: Causal Plan for Benchmarking and Building Physically Grounded Embodied Reasoners
items.summary: Current benchmarks for embodied vision-language planning inadvertently favor linguistic next-token prediction over physically grounded next-state reasoning. This rewards models that mimic statistical language priors rather than track true causal dependencies, reducing complex physical planning to shallow sequence modeling. Hence, achieving genuine physical autonomy requires a fundamental shift from linguistically grounded token prediction toward physically grounded causal reasoning. To this end, we introduce Causal-Plan-Bench, a high-fidelity diagnostic suite spanning four causal dimensions, curated via multi-stage verification. To endow models with this capability, a four-stage annotation pipeline extracts structured interaction records from egocentric videos to construct Causal-Plan-1M, a dense million-scale corpus of explicit causal reasoning traces. Extensive evaluation reveals a striking gap: leading models struggle to demonstrate genuine physical agency -- even GPT-6-astra scores only 43.04. In contrast, our tailored training recipe enables Causal Planner to internalize the complex physical logic required for accurate next-state estimation. Built upon Qwen3-VL-8B, Causal Planner raises its backbone's score from 33.23 to 45.28, a 36.3% relative gain, and improves on three external benchmarks without benchmark-specific adaptation. items.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies leverage pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to guide action generation for robot control. VLMs provide hierarchical visual-semantic representations that evolve across layers, from local visual geometry to abstract, language-aligned semantics; different manipulation tasks may therefore require different mixtures of layer representations. Meanwhile, the action module maintains intermediate representations that evolve throughout action computation and may provide useful information for subsequent decisions. However, existing VLA interfaces offer limited flexibility in representation access: VLM information is exposed through fixed layer assignments for each action layer, while intermediate action states are only propagated implicitly through residual streams without explicit reuse. We introduce LayerRoute, an action-conditioned representation routing interface that enables adaptive access to VLM layers and action representations. The Layer Mixture Router dynamically forms mixtures of cached VLM representations, while Action-State Reread reuses earlier action representations. Across diverse simulation and real-world benchmarks, LayerRoute consistently improves StarVLA-$\pi$ and $\pi_{0.5}$, achieving up to 7.2 gains on LIBERO Long with only 0.31% / 3.87% additional parameters. items.title: Agentic AI with Structured CoT for Enhancing AI's Spatial Intelligence: Visualization and Reasoning of Rotation
items.summary: Recent studies show that artificial intelligence (AI) with language and vision capabilities still experiences limitations in spatial reasoning. items.title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
items.summary: Video generative models offer a promising basis for robotic planning by predicting future visual rollouts from observations and task instructions. However, their training objectives typically lack explicit constraints on robot executability. Generated rollouts can exhibit embodiment-related artifacts, including arm deformation and temporal discontinuities, while the actions decoded from these rollouts may be unstable or violate robot motion limits. We term this mismatch between generated robot behavior and embodiment-specific execution requirements the executability gap. We introduce Executable Video Alignment (EVA), a post-training framework that uses action-space feedback to improve both the visual integrity of generated robot motion and the feasibility of decoded actions. EVA trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on robot demonstrations and freezes it to decode actions from generated videos. We compute a reward from these actions that penalizes non-smooth motion and violations of velocity and acceleration limits, and use it to guide reinforcement-learning updates to the video generator. By feeding decoded-action constraints back into video generation, EVA links visual and action-level improvements through a shared alignment signal. items.title: LIBERO-Pro2.0: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of Embodied Foundation Models

items.title: LynxScenes: A Large-Scale Real-World Benchmark for Outdoor Wheel-Legged Robot Perception, Navigation, Imagination and Reconstruction

items.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos
items.summary: Long videos often exceed the context capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), while agentic search repeats costly video processing and grounding for each query. items.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
items.summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on this observation, we introduce VLA-Rolling, a lightweight inference framework that reuses action tails through three stages: action-tail inheritance, per-action confidence estimation, and confidence-guided refinement through renoising and denoising budget allocation, while the underlying VLA remains frozen. Across $\pi_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, X-VLA, and MolmoAct2 on LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, VLA-Rolling reduces action-chunk inference cost in all 16 model--benchmark pairs, achieving up to a $1.48\times$ speedup, while improving success rate in 14 pairs by up to $15.08$ percentage points. items.title: SPAR: Structural Pruning and Action Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: The limited onboard computing resources of robots make the inference demands of vision-language-action (VLA) models costly to accommodate. Reducing these demands through aggressive compression, however, can degrade manipulation performance beyond what supervised fine-tuning alone recovers. We present SPAR (Structural Pruning and Action Recovery), which simultaneously prunes the hidden and feed-forward intermediate dimensions of the large language model (LLM) backbone through pruning-aware tuning, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to recover policy performance. Applied to $\pi_{0.5}$, SPAR reduces the language backbone from 2.34B to 0.09B parameters and the full model from 3.37B to 1.12B, removing approximately 96% and 67% of their parameters, respectively. At this compression level, RL raises average success across the four LIBERO suites from 84.55% to 93.45%, an 8.90-percentage-point gain. The compressed policy achieves a $1.98\times$ full-policy inference speedup over the unpruned model. These results identify substantial intermediate-dimension redundancy and show that post-pruning RL can recover manipulation performance in compact policies.

items.title: VQActFlow: Vector-Quantized Action Mode Steering for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Multi-task robot manipulation policies are challenging to learn from demonstration because traditionally a single network must select among qualitatively different action modes from a multimodal demonstration distribution, conditioned on language and visual context. A wrong mode selection means executing the wrong task or an action infeasible in the scene. Tokenizing continuous actions into a learned discrete codebook separates these modes at the representation level, offering structural advantages for multi-task learning. We propose VQActFlow, a multi-task manipulation policy that tokenizes action chunks and generates code sequences via Variational Flow Matching. VQActFlow maintains an explicit preference over action modes throughout generation. Inference-time guidance acts on this preference to steer mode commitment. We instantiate this with classifier-free guidance over language conditioning, which steers the policy toward the instructed action mode, and a learned codebook critic that supplies a complementary feasibility signal. We evaluate VQActFlow on three platforms: the LIBERO simulation benchmarks, a Unitree G1 humanoid performing whole-body pick-and-place, and an ALOHA-style bimanual platform performing contact-rich tasks. Across these benchmarks, VQActFlow outperforms both continuous and discrete baselines.

items.title: Learning When to Trust and Reobserve Sparse-Frame VideoQA from Temporal Sampling Perturbations
items.summary: Sparse-frame video-language models can change their answers when only the sampling timestamps shift. Raw agreement exposes this problem, but it need not rank errors better than token confidence or identify which additional observation will repair an answer. items.title: Memory Forcing: Attendable Mid-Horizon History for Streaming Video Generation
items.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion enables causal video streaming without a bidirectional pass over the full clip, but existing few-step systems usually retain only the opening and most recent frames in a fixed-size KV cache. Once an event leaves this window, later frames can no longer attend to it, a failure we term mid-horizon forgetting. We present Memory Forcing, a few-step streaming method that preserves this missing history without increasing the cache size. Its Archive \& Working Banks partition the cache into sink, archive, and working regions, retaining diverse intermediate events alongside recent motion under fixed memory. Because absolute temporal indices drift outside the training range, Bank-aware RoPE reassigns indices at attention time so each bank remains distinguishable. At 1.3B, Memory Forcing leads on longer clips, shows the smallest drop from 5s to 60s among methods reporting all four lengths, and preserves subjects and scenes through leave-and-return. The same design scales to Wan2.2 5B, producing more physically plausible, realistic, and dynamic videos and, to our knowledge, the first public 5B model on this forcing line.

items.summary: Video Question Grounding (VideoQG) requires both accurate question answering and precise temporal localization. Finally, we introduce Semantic Diff Refinement, a training-free temporal refinement method that exploits semantic differences between neighboring SigLIP2 embeddings to recover complete action segments from sparse predictions. Extensive experiments on NExT-GQA and STAR show that DiffGround consistently outperforms existing zero-shot and supervised methods, establishing a new state of the art for Video Question Grounding.

items.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
items.summary: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. items.title: Preserving the Manifold: Frozen Expert Alignment for Label-Efficient SAR Scene Understanding

items.title: RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models
items.summary: Genuine embodied agency requires robots to turn continuous real-world experience into lasting, transferable skills. This demands continual learning that integrates new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge in evolving environments. Experience replay mitigates catastrophic forgetting, but storing complete demonstrations becomes costly as tasks accumulate. World-action models provide an alternative through generative replay. However, visually coherent rollouts may contain actions that cannot realize the predicted transitions, while new-task adaptation can disrupt learned behavior. To address these problems, we propose RIFAR (Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay), a reliability-informed and drift-aware generative replay framework. It reconstructs trajectories from compact historical demonstration prefixes and uses a trainable inverse-dynamics model to assess action-visual consistency. It first adapts to new tasks using current-task demonstrations and high-reliability replay, then evaluates how this adaptation changes action predictions on historical inputs and prioritizes reliable trajectories with greater action drift for further training. Across three LIBERO suites and real-world experiments, RIFAR outperforms the previous state of the art in WAM-based generative replay. On LIBERO-Goal, it achieves an AUC of 90.97 while retaining only 320 historical time...
rationale: Matched: world action model, dynamics model, embodied, robot learning

items.title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout...
rationale: Matched: keypoint, vision language action, vla, robotic manipulation

items.title: From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are asked to report what they see: to count objects, box them, parse a screen or pick a click target (GUI grounding). We argue that reporting is part of the visual task, not merely its formatting. In a dense scene with 173 shapes, GPT-6.1 lists 173 records that match every shape, yet the counts it states in the same response sum to 188. From Seeing to Reporting (FSR) is a theory of visual reporting and a set of inference-time procedures that improve the reports of frozen VLMs. It models reporting as a chain from responses to decoded records, constructed sets and task answers, linked by task-compatible matching. The chain gives exact relations for deleting records, averaging their coordinates and switching readouts, and it splits the error of one answer chosen among several calls into missing candidates, lost representatives and wrong choices. These relations guide procedures for counting, detection, document layout, screen parsing and GUI grounding that use the task specification and a shipped configuration, without requiring labels from the target task. On 50 dense synthetic scenes, a one-call reporting-and-decoding protocol cuts per-type count error by 85.2% for GPT-6.1 and 98.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5. On 600 ScreenSpot-Pro items, a GUI-grounding tier that combines three models lowers the miss rate from 13.67% for GPT-6.1's two-stage zoom to...
